column1: # Player-facing settings: the iOS launcher (dm/ios/Sources/Launcher.swift) and the Mac app's settings window (dm/mac/Launcher.swift) show them before the game starts; Mac front ends read the same list.

# dm/games/settings.py writes one game's list into its app (dm/launcher.json; build_ipa.sh, and dm/mac/pack_app.py through the NSP script): the rows whose condition holds for that game, with its defaults. Each sets an environment variable the host reads when the game starts; one an env file sets
# (Documents/env.txt, the bundle's dm/env.txt) is shown but kept. Diagnostic switches stay environment-only, so they are not listed here. The player's page is docs/settings.md.
#   variable  the environment variable the setting sets
#   kind      choice: values value=label,... (languages: the game's own, from its control data); range: values low:high:step, shown as a percentage;
#             toggle: values - (on sets 1, off 0) or <on>/<off>, the two values the variable takes (on/off)
#   default   a value (a toggle's: 1 on, 0 off); DM_GAME_<NAME>: the host's own default from the game profile (game_profile.h, game.py); build:<VAR>: the IPA build's setting (build_ipa.sh)
#             <ios>|<mac> selects the platform's default before resolving a profile macro or build variable

#   shown     always; DM_GAME_<NAME>!=<value> or ==<value>; fixups:<KEY>: main's rewriter table has that key (a stub in the game's build, patch_nso.py); languages>1; gfxapi:<API>: the packer's GFXAPI; platform:<ios | mac>: the app's platform (SETTINGS_PLATFORM, ios when unset), for a switch only that platform's front end reads
#   section   Game, Graphics, Controls or Performance: a heading on the single settings screen. Rows appear in table order within each section
#             Reset to tested defaults clears all launcher choices; values fixed by an env file stay
#   label, note  the setting's name and the line under it (may be empty; only for a setting with a cost: latency, memory, heat)
#   meta      optional, key=value pairs separated by ; (settings.py META lists the keys; docs/frontends.md, The settings list, describes them):
#             level=basic  a setting a front end shows first;  needs=<VAR>=<value>  a sub-setting, drawn only while the row that sets <VAR> has that value

column8: The game's own languages; the app starts in the one packed with the IPA.
Window for the desktop; Fullscreen fills the display.
Shows the frames put on screen per second at the top left.
60 fps is smoother; 30 fps uses less power and keeps the phone cooler.
Lower renders fewer pixels: lighter on the GPU but softer. Text and the interface stay sharp.
Docked uses the TV resolution (sharper); Handheld uses the handheld resolution (lighter).
Lowers resolution between 70% and 100% under load instead of dropping frames.
MetalFX sharpens the scaled picture; it uses more GPU time and can add heat.
A light tap when you press an on-screen button.
The game's vibration on the phone or on a connected controller.
How strong the game's vibration is, from 0 to 300%.
Ignores weak controller rumble below this level; the phone's vibration is not affected.
Copies each frame so the GPU starts the next at once; up to one frame more display latency.
In order is smoother; Newest frame can reduce lag but may look uneven.
Keeps a pipeline archive and builds most pipelines from bases; uses more memory.
Prepares pipelines before the first frame; the first start waits a few minutes, once.
Translates graphics commands on their own thread, so the game's thread can go on sooner.
In heavy scenes, drops to half the frame rate instead of showing uneven late frames.
Apple's overlay with fps, frame and GPU time and memory; leave it off to play.
